# Gobbl

> Gobbl is a free, open-source (MIT) notch app for Mac, made by Xeve (https://xeve.io). It lives in the MacBook notch with a pet mascot, Gob: a small retro computer with a face on its screen, in three models (Classic, Compact, Candy). It runs on macOS 14 or later. Macs without a notch get a pill at the top of the screen instead. There is no Windows or Linux version.

Key facts:
- Price: free. The AI features (writing, chat, briefs, Polish with AI, Memory to-dos) are free during the beta and will become a paid plan later. Optional one-time "pay what you want" support payment (suggested $20): https://gobbl.xeve.io/support
- Open source: https://github.com/xeveio/gobbl (MIT license). No account, and no analytics in the app.
- Notch basics:
  - drag-and-drop file shelf with file tools (convert, compress, remove background, copy text, zip);
  - clipboard history on Shift-Command-Space;
  - Now Playing with synced lyrics;
  - volume, brightness and Caps Lock HUDs;
  - calendar with Join links;
  - focus timer, keep-awake and quick tools.
- The pet: moods, eyes that follow the cursor, types along with you, Matrix rain while AI coding agents work, unboxing, 11 hats, streaks and levels, shareable .gobskin skins and 6-second clips.
- AI agents: Claude Code, Codex and Grok status in the notch, in a terminal or through an editor or desktop app. Claude Code permission requests can be allowed or denied from the notch (it falls back to the terminal after 30 seconds). Codex runs only hooks the user has approved, so Gobbl's hooks must be approved once with /hooks in Codex, or under Hooks in Codex's settings in the editor.
- Gobbl key (right Option): tap to write or rewrite in any text field; double-tap for edit mode with versions (shorter, friendlier, and more); hold to dictate; type /g plus a question to get an answer.
- Dictation:
  - on-device Whisper, and audio never leaves the Mac;
  - about 0.5 s per sentence on Apple silicon;
  - Verbatim, Light and Polish with AI clean-up;
  - custom words, language lock and hands-free mode;
  - no word cap and no account;
  - needs Apple silicon.
- Chat: reminders in plain English, a morning brief and an evening wrap, pre-meeting briefs 10 minutes before meetings with people Gobbl knows, and at most 3 gentle nudges a day.
- Memory (opt-in beta):
  - reads on-screen text through macOS Accessibility, never screenshots, and stores it on the Mac only;
  - masks secrets, and skips password fields, private windows and banking sites;
  - finds to-dos that tick themselves off when proof appears (with Undo);
  - a Memory window with to-dos, a timeline with day digests, and people, project, organisation and topic cards;
  - search by meaning on-device (Apple sentence embeddings), and a memory chat with cited sources;
  - pause and forget controls.
- MCP connector (available, part of the Memory beta): one switch ("Connect AI apps automatically") registers the gobbl-mcp helper with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex (also covers the ChatGPT desktop app), Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, LM Studio and Zed. Read tools: search_memory, get_day, list_todos, who_is, get_person, get_project, recent_activity. Via the running app: get_clipboard, add_reminder, mark_todo_done. Answers cite sources; each call is logged on the Mac by tool name and time only.
- Privacy: local first. AI requests go through Xeve's service to a provider that doesn't keep data, and every request is logged on the Mac.
